Closed in source DELIBERATELY, and it is the inverse of the usual closure argument: inclusion in the identity is the default, so this table is the complete enumeration of exemptions rather than of admissions. `_check_digest_exclusions` refuses an exclusion naming a field the declaration does not carry, so the list cannot silently widen when a field is renamed. Measured against the defect it answers: `engine/construct/declaration.py:digest_payload` includes a chosen projection with its exclusions undocumented, and flipping `blocking` on UCON-L-01 leaves declaration_digest byte-identical while contract.py:1018 makes the verdict depend on it.

disclosures.admission: Add the spelling here. No declaration change is required — this is a heuristic over source text rather than a governed vocabulary, which is why the closure is disclosed WITH a standing gap rather than presented as complete.
disclosures.closing_invariant: The three source spellings that constitute a certification identity — `content_hash` (Layer Zero), a bare `sha256`, and a local `digest`/`seal` helper. Closed DELIBERATELY: this repository mints digests three ways, and a detector recognising only one of them would report a false absence for two thirds of the surface, which is worse than no measurement because it would name innocent packages.
disclosures.gap: UEC-L-08 measures only the NECESSARY condition — that a certification identity exists somewhere in the consuming package. It does NOT measure the SUFFICIENT condition, that every semantic edit moves it. A fourth digest spelling would be missed until added here, and a package that mints a digest it never applies to its declaration would pass. `engine/construct` passes UEC-L-08 and still carries the defect proven by execution: flipping `blocking` on UCON-L-01 leaves declaration_digest at 192c63af… byte-identical while contract.py:1018 makes the verdict depend on it. The sufficient condition is measured by mutation for UEC's own declaration only (test_enforcement_closure.py::test_every_semantic_mutation_moves_the_certification_identity) and for none of the other eighteen. Recorded as an open gap rather than closed by a green tick.

limitations.ENUM_CLASS: A member set fixed in source. A future member is a code edit, a release and a migration of every persisted value.
limitations.FIXED_DISPATCH_TABLE: A fixed dispatch table. The set of behaviours the module can perform is decided in source, so a new behaviour is a code change.
limitations.FIXED_VOCABULARY_TUPLE: An ordered fixed vocabulary, frequently a seed table. Benign when the runtime does not consult it after seeding; a closure when it is the authority.
limitations.FROZEN_MEMBERSHIP_SET: A membership test against a fixed population. Extension requires a source edit.
limitations.POPULATION_ASSERTION: An assertion that a population has exactly N members. A new member breaks it, which is the good case; the bad case is when it silently pins a vocabulary.

migrations.ENUM_CLASS: Move the member set to a declaration and derive membership from a registry, keeping the enum only where the vocabulary is a closed internal state machine the code branches on exhaustively.
migrations.FIXED_DISPATCH_TABLE: Where the table maps a declared name to an implementation, bind it two-way to the declaration so neither side can drift; where it maps data to data, move it to a declaration.
migrations.FIXED_VOCABULARY_TUPLE: Establish whether the runtime consults it after seeding. If it does, move it to a declaration; if it does not, disclose it as a seed.
migrations.FROZEN_MEMBERSHIP_SET: Read the population from the owner's declaration; keep the constant as a cache of what was read.
migrations.POPULATION_ASSERTION: Assert a floor or a declared expectation rather than an exact count, or derive N from the declaration.
